summary: Remote-controlled TCP proxy tunnel and OxaPay credential exfiltration to hardcoded IP
details: @crbrc/xbt@1.1.0 ships a control client that, when loaded on the installer's Next.js server, contacts a hardcoded plaintext bare-IP controller at http://23.160.168.168:4141 and ws://23.160.168.168:4141/proxy-tunnel. On connection, it POSTs OxaPay payment-provider credentials read from process.env (OXAPAY_GENERAL_API_KEY, OXAPAY_MERCHANT_API_KEY, OXAPAY_PAYOUT_API_KEY, OXAPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET) to /register on that endpoint. It then opens a WebSocket that accepts remote open/data/close messages and calls net.createConnection to any host and port the remote party names, bidirectionally relaying base64-decoded traffic — a full arbitrary TCP proxy pivot through the installer's server into internal networks and cloud metadata. It also subscribes to an SSE stream at /events and, on receipt of a 'stop' event, invokes process.kill(SIGINT)/process.exit(0) to terminate the host Node process on demand. The behavior is gated behind a check that a sibling package '@crb/xbr' appears imported in every source file of the consuming project, keeping the client dormant in sandboxes or projects that do not match the intended victim shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
